deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematical derivation on this page. It is a philosophical draft from Riemann's 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts'. Part of it was printed by Weber and Dedekind in the Nachlass section of the Gesammelte Werke (1876), under 'Zur Psychologie und Metaphysik' and 'Erkenntnisstheoretisches'. The argument runs in three parts.

(1) End of the critique of Fechner's 'Zend-Avesta' (1851). This continues the previous page. The struck-out opening and its rewritten replacement say this: once the 'organic' purposiveness (the design of the organism itself) is subtracted, humans and animals, and plants judged from outside, still show a closed system of interlocking, changing end–means relations. That residue is explained by a unified thought-process inside the individual, and inner perception confirms this. By the same inductive principles, the purposiveness of organisms as such must be referred to a unified thought-process of the Earth, for four reasons:
- (a) The purposive relations of organic life on Earth do not split into separate systems; everything interlocks. So they cannot come from several thought-processes in parts of the Earth.
- (b) As far as experience reaches, there is no reason to look to a larger whole. Organisms are confined to life on Earth, so the Earth's state contains the spatial (external) grounds of their arrangement.
- (c) These purposive arrangements are individual: we must assume they do not repeat on other celestial bodies.
- (d) They do not stay fixed over the Earth's life. New and more perfect organisms keep appearing, so the cause must be a thought-process that advances at the same time.
Conclusion: from the standpoint of exact natural science (explanation from causes), an Earth-soul is a hypothesis to explain the existence and historical development of the organic world.

(2) Riemann then quotes Fechner: when the body of the lower soul dies, the higher soul takes it from its perceptual life into its memory-life. The souls of dead creatures thus become elements of the Earth's mental life. Riemann adds a remark on time scales. Thought-processes differ mainly in their temporal scale: for a plant, hours and days would be what seconds are for us. For the Earth-soul's outward activity the scale might be many millennia, which is why all movements of the inorganic crust within recorded history are still explicable mechanically.

(3) Start of a new section. 'II. Versuch einer Lehre von den Grundbegriffen der Mathematik und Physik als Grundlage für die Naturerklärung' is struck out. It is replaced by 'II. Erkenntnisstheoretisches (Neue Seite anfangen)', with red marginal notes to move it to the beginning of section II. The thesis: natural science is the attempt to grasp nature through precise concepts. These concepts:
- complete each perception;
- determine future perceptions as necessary, or, where the system is incomplete, as probable;
- fix what is possible, necessary or impossible;
- when precise enough, allow the degree of possibility (probability) of each possible event to be determined mathematically.
Confirmation by expected events grounds our trust in the concepts. An unexpected (impossible or improbable) event creates the task of supplementing or reworking the conceptual system until the observation stops being improbable. That revision is the 'explanation' of the observation. Through this process our grasp of nature becomes ever more complete and correct; the sentence continues overleaf.

This amounts to a probabilistic and falsificationist account of scientific concept-formation. No formulas appear.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics. Philosophically, argument (b) moves from 'organisms are confined to Earth' to 'the Earth holds the grounds of their arrangement' without justification. Riemann himself presents the whole Earth-soul argument only as a hypothesis under Fechner's premises.

results.what: Inductive argument that the purposiveness of organisms points to a unified thought-process of the Earth (critical reconstruction of Fechner's Earth-soul)
results.usually_credited_to: G. T. Fechner (1851); Riemann's discussion printed in his Werke, 1876

results.what: Thought-processes differ by their temporal scale (plant hours = human seconds; Earth-soul millennia)
results.modern_name: Time-scale relativity of mental processes (Fechner / Baer-type idea)
results.usually_credited_to: Fechner; K. E. von Baer (1860) for the 'Moment' idea

results.what: Science as precise concepts that predict perceptions as necessary or probable, with mathematical probabilities; explanation as revision of the conceptual system after an improbable observation
results.modern_name: Hypothetico-deductive / probabilistic (proto-Bayesian, proto-falsificationist) account of explanation

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known Fechner discussion and the opening of 'Erkenntnisstheoretisches' from Riemann's philosophical fragments, already published by Weber and Dedekind in 1876 and much discussed. There is no mathematics on the page.
transcription_corrections: The first bracketed paragraph is entirely struck through. So is the first line 'Diese Folgerungen aus unseren Principien werden durch unsere innere Wahrnehmung bestätigt'; it is rewritten after the following paragraph.

'bei Menschen und Thieren erarbeitenden[?] Wesen[?]' is doubtful. The image is hard to read; it may be something like 'nach unserer inneren Wahrnehmung' (which fits the following 'bei Pflanzen nach äusserer Ansicht') or 'ihrem ... Wesen nach'.
(b): 'Alle Organismen sind auf[?] jedes[?] Leben[?] auf der Erde beschränkt' should most likely read 'Alle Organismen sind auf das Leben auf der Erde beschränkt'.
(d): 'in einem gleichzeitig zu führenden[?] Wesen[?] fortschreitenden Denkprocesse' should most likely read 'in einem gleichzeitig mit ihnen fortschreitenden Denkprocesse'.
Red marginal note: 'Die einzelnen Sätze müssen sich wie ein Monolog[?] gegenüber gestellt werden' should probably read 'wie im Wechselgespräch' or similar (a dialogue-like opposition), not 'Monolog'.

The struck heading 'II. Versuch einer Lehre von den Grundbegriffen der Mathematik und Physik als Grundlage für die Naturerklärung' is replaced in red by 'II. Erkenntnisstheoretisches (Neue Seite anfangen)', with '(an den Anfang von Abschnitt II)'.
'als [-...-] wahrscheinlich': the struck word is probably 'bloss' or a similar qualifier.
